summary: The proposal fails to address critical performance and accessibility risks associated with the current implementation of the art viewer and its transition logic.

items.issue: Potential memory leak and performance degradation due to uncontrolled interval timers in ArtViewer.
items.evidence: src/art/ArtViewer.tsx: The setInterval for the 60-second rotation depends on [playing, paused, visible, failed, loaded, selected.id]. Frequent state updates to these dependencies will repeatedly clear and restart the interval, resetting the 250ms tick and potentially causing jitter in elapsed time calculation.
items.change: Move the timing logic into a dedicated useInterval hook or use a requestAnimationFrame loop to ensure smooth time accumulation independent of React render cycles.
items.check: Verify that elapsed.current increments linearly without jumps during state updates to other viewer properties.

items.issue: Accessibility failure: The ArtViewer dialog lacks a proper focus trap and relies on autoFocus on a 'Close' button, which may disrupt screen reader navigation of the artwork content.
items.evidence: src/art/ArtViewer.tsx: <dialog ... onCancel={onClose} onClose={onClose}> ... <button type="button" onClick={onClose} autoFocus>Close artwork</button></dialog>
items.change: Implement a robust focus trap that allows navigation through the controls (Previous, Next, Select) before hitting the Close button, and ensure the dialog is correctly labeled for assistive technology.
items.check: Test with a screen reader to ensure the user is not immediately forced to the Close button upon opening the viewer.

items.issue: Fragile image event handling: The 'ready' state depends on the onLoad event, which may not fire for cached images in some browser environments, leading to a stale image or a stuck transition.
items.change: Check the .complete property of the image element inside a useEffect hook immediately after mounting to handle cached images that have already loaded.
items.check: Verify that artworks load and transition immediately when served from the browser cache.
